title: Run policy
description: The document that narrows what one run may do. Read once from a file outside the checkout, or from the security_policy of a server's run configuration, and pinned for the run. It can only tighten what the Forager binary allows; it never grants: a credential, a tool or an image it selects is one the machine defines, and it defines none.

version.description: The policy format. Forager refuses a version it does not read.

egress.description: What the session may reach through the gateway.

mode.description: observe records every connection and denies only what deny covers; enforce denies a connection to a host outside allow and allow_first as well, and records the denial. Enforce with no allow list reaches only the hosts allow_first lists.

allow.description: Hosts the session may reach: a lower-case host name, or a *. suffix matching every host below it and not the apex itself. No ports, no paths, no schemes: paths have a separate key. Absent means an empty list.

allow_first.description: Hosts the session may reach in either mode, checked before deny and allow: a lower-case host name or an IPv4 address in canonical form, with no *. pattern. A host an entry matches is allowed and recorded with the entry as its rule; a host below an entry is not matched. The guard, wall:host-form, wall:plain-request, the run limits and paths still apply. In a policy that narrows another, an entry lifts only the deny and allow of the policy that lists it. Absent means an empty list.

deny.description: Hosts the session may not reach, in allow's grammar, in either mode: a host an entry here covers is denied before allow and before the mode are consulted, unless allow_first lists the host, and the denial is recorded with the entry as its rule. Absent means an empty list.

paths.description: The paths the session may request on a host, by host in allow's grammar. A host several entries cover is held to the most specific one: its name itself, else the *. entry with the longest suffix. A host listed here is one the proxy terminates TLS for, behind a wall, because a path is inside the connection: a request whose path no entry matches is denied under enforce and recorded either way, and a host not listed is reached on every path. A path is compared as the server reads it, case and all; a request whose path could be read two ways is denied.

additionalProperties.description: An empty list is no path of the host at all.

credentials.description: The credentials of the machine's this run may use, by name, behind a wall. The gateway keeps each outside the enclosure and sets it on the requests to the hosts it is for, which it terminates TLS for; the session's environment and files contain at most a placeholder for it. A name the machine does not define is no run.

argument.description: What the run requests of the credential, such as a repository, passed to the definition's adapter as one argument. The definition sets what an argument may look like; one it does not provide for is no run. At most 4096 characters, which leaves room for several repositories in one argument, acme/shop,acme/lib. The cap bounds only the size of the run's record, not what the argument may contain: what guards it is the definition's pattern, which must match it whole, and it reaches the program as one word, with no shell.

tools.description: The tools of the machine's this run may reach, by name, behind a wall. The gateway starts each for the run outside the enclosure; the proxy terminates TLS for the hosts it serves and sends it every request to them that it allows, including under observe those whose path no rule covers, which are recorded as allowed with an empty path_rule. A name the machine does not define is no run.

argument.description: What the run requests of the tool, such as a repository or a prefix, passed to the definition's command as one argument. The definition sets what an argument may look like; one it does not provide for is no run. At most 4096 characters, which leaves room for several repositories in one argument, acme/shop,acme/lib. The cap bounds only the size of the run's record, not what the argument may contain: what guards it is the definition's pattern, which must match it whole, and it reaches the program as one word, with no shell.

image.description: The image the run starts in, behind a wall: the machine's name for one of its images, or a reference pinned by digest, NAME@sha256: and 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits, under one of the machine's images.allow prefixes. The machine defines its images, a reference and the runtime the wall starts each under, and the prefixes it allows; the policy selects one and defines none. Absent means the machine's default. A name the machine does not define is no run, image_unknown; a reference with a tag, in upper case or without a digest is no run, run_configuration_invalid, before the schema reads it; a reference under none of the prefixes is no run, image_not_allowed. The image is fixed when the run starts.

host_entry.description: A host entry of egress.allow, and of a run configuration's stack_hosts: a lower-case host name or an IPv4 address, or a *. suffix matching every host below it and not the apex itself. No port, no path, no scheme.

image_name.description: The machine's name for one of its images: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, underscore, dot and dash, starting with a letter or a digit.

image_reference.description: An image pinned by its digest: NAME, then @sha256:, then 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits. NAME is a lower-case OCI reference name: an optional registry host followed by a slash, then one or more path components separated by slashes. The host is lower-case DNS labels separated by dots, each of lower-case ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, with an optional port of 1 to 5 digits after a colon. Each path component is lower-case ASCII letters and digits, with a dot, an underscore, two underscores or one or more hyphens between two runs of them. NAME is at most 255 characters, so the whole value is at most 327. A tag, such as :latest, and upper case are refused, so the value names one build and never moves.

path.description: A path from the root, matched whole, or up to a final * matched as a prefix: /repos/acme/shop, /repos/acme/shop/*. No other wildcard, no query.
